title: Twilight handoff crib notes
content:
Purpose: quick, practical handoff for twilight/overnight. Not polished — scribbles + command snippets. Use as temporary runbook until we merge into the official playbook.

Key context (TL;DR):
- Tonight: rolling canary for model v3.1 started at 21:00 UTC; 30% traffic. Watch latencies for /generate on dedicated pools.
- Recent flakiness in autoscaler causing delayed pod spin-ups (~3–5m). Workaround: manual scale or route to fallback pool.
- Storage-I/O alert spiked twice today on serving-runtime-us-west; engineering ticket INF-2142 (linked) tracks follow-up.

Immediate checks (first 5 minutes):
- Slack: #oncall-twilight, #serving-runtime. Ping if you take action.
- Check SLO dashboard: /console/slo -> look at p50/p95/p99 for generate and embeddings.
- Alerts: alertmanager -> query active alerts: ring buffer, autoscaler-delay, high-kv-cache-miss. If more than 2 concurrent, escalate to SRE lead (Liam).

Common incident patterns + quick fixes:
1) High p95/p99 latency on /generate (hosted/dedicated)
  - Quick inspect: curl -sS https://metrics.internal/api/latency?route=generate&last=10m
  - If backend GPUs maxed (util > 95% across pool):
    * TEMP fix: shift 20% traffic to fallback pool: POST /routing/api/traffic-shift {model:v3.1, percent:20, target:fallback-pool}
    * If fallback not available, scale up dedicated nodes (manual): kubectl -n serving scale deployment/gpu-pool-xx --replicas=+2 (confirm quotas first)
  - Note: scaling often delayed due to nodegroup limit; if autoscaler flapping, open INF ticket and use reroute.

2) OOMs on model servers after a rollout
  - Symptoms: OOMKilled pods, repeated restarts, model load failures in logs (OOM while allocating KV cache).
  - Quick mitigation: rollback canary to previous model: flow-> console -> model rollbacks -> choose v3.0 immediate (or run CLI: rwoodctl model rollback --id v3.1 --to v3.0)
  - If rollback blocked, set model max_seq=1024 in runtime config to reduce memory footprint.

3) Autoscaler not adding pods (stuck in Pending)
  - Check events: kubectl describe nodegroup/gpu-ng-xx -> look for resource quotas or taints.
  - If image pull errors: kubectl logs pod/xxx -n serving -> /docker/pull error -> try force recreate node: kubectl delete pod/xxx --grace-period=0 (kube will reschedule).

4) Prefix/KV cache regression (seen as cache-miss rate spike)
  - Symptom: higher token cost and latency for repeated prefixes.
  - Quick check: metrics cache_hit_ratio last 30m; if <0.6, restart cache-worker job in namespace cache-service.
  - Note to next shift: there is a known flaky job (cache-evictor) — patch in PR #4677 (linked in INF-2142).

Operational commands I use (copy/paste with care):
- View last 2h alerts: curl -s https://alertmanager.internal/api/alerts?since=2h | jq '.'
- Traffic shift (temporary): rwoodctl routing shift --model v3.1 --from 30 --to 10 --target fallback-pool --reason "night shift mitigation"
- Rollback (CLI): rwoodctl model rollback --name redwood/gpt-3.1 --to redwood/gpt-3.0 --force
- Scale pool (k8s): kubectl -n serving scale deployment/gpu-pool-usw-3 --replicas=6

Notes to next engineer (explicit):
- If you have to reboot serve-gpu-12, do it in this order: drain -> wait for 2 healthy in pool -> reboot -> verify model endpoint comes back with 200 on /health. Reboots in parallel caused 503s last week.
- Avoid applying patch ops/quickfix/v2 unless ops approves; it bypasses canary rules and has caused double-routing before.
- There is a shelved experiment (experiment/kv-adaptive) that sometimes re-enables itself; if you see unexpected cache parameters, check flagstore: /flags/kv-adaptive and set to false.

Open tasks (follow-ups):
- Confirm autoscaler bug triage owner (assigned to @pri on JIRA but need confirmation).
- Add playbook section for manual traffic shifts into official runbook (tickets: DOCS-95).
- Clean up stale fallback pools list in routing service (one pool points to decommissioned infra).

Escalation/contact list (night):
- Primary SRE: Liam O'Connor (pager)
- Secondary: Priya Singh (slack/phone)
- Platform Eng lead: Arjun Patel (for infra quotas)

Misc tips & trivia (from tonight):
- When debugging model load failures, grep logs for "KV cache shard" — that string shows exact shard ID causing OOM.
- If a route shows 100% 502s but pods healthy: check ingress TLS termination cert rotation job (rotates at 03:00 UTC). If it failed earlier, restarting ingress controller fixed it.
- Keyboard shortcuts: console quick jump: press 'g' then type model id to open model details (small life-saver).

Anything else: scribble here. If you take an action, please add a 1–2 line note at the top with timestamp and short summary so we have a mini audit trail.

---
Recent action log (example entries):
- 2026-03-12 21:05 UTC — Maya: shifted 20% traffic from canary to fallback-pool after p95 hit 1.8s. Notified #oncall-twilight.
- 2026-03-12 21:22 UTC — Maya: scaled gpu-pool-usw-3 to 6 replicas temporarily; confirmed latency drop to p95 0.9s.

TODO (next improvements):
- Turn this into a checklist template and push to /confluence/Serving+Runtime+Quick+Playbook.
- Add one-liner rollback commands to the secured cli snippets vault.

Questions (left unresolved):
- Why did the autoscaler record CPU>threshold but not spin nodes? Need nodegroup metrics correlated — left for next-day triage.
- Does the fallback pool have the same quantization profile? If not, token cost differences will appear; check config: /configs/quant-profiles.

End of crib notes. Good luck and ping me if things look off.
